A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same HopCast study, with 22 readable pages including Appendices A–J. Text comparison and page rendering establish that pages 3–22 are identical; differences on pages 1–2 concern publication-status text and reflow.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on five simulated dynamical systems, including calibration errors and prediction-interval widths in Table 1, MSE results in Appendix H, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original five-system experiments, the results in Tables 1 and 3, and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same deterministic base model, Modern Hopfield Network residual learning, context construction, training procedure, and inference through residual sampling.

E1.justification: Both versions use Lotka–Volterra, Lorenz, FitzHugh–Nagumo, Lorenz95, and the glycolytic oscillator under the same noise conditions. The heteroscedastic sine-function demonstration in Appendix G is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain the same comparators: deterministic ensembles and probabilistic ensembles using Expectation, Moment Matching, or Trajectory Sampling.

E3.justification: Data generation, splits, noise levels, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and tuning procedures are unchanged, including the settings in Appendices C, F, and I.

E4.justification: The sequence-length and attention-span study in Appendix G and the residual-density, predictive-distribution, and calibration analyses in Appendix J are identical. No ablation or robustness evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain identical ± reporting. There are no changes to repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimation, confidence intervals, or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All calibration-error, prediction-interval-width, and MSE entries in Tables 1 and 3 are identical. The reported rankings, qualitative findings, and plotted results in Appendices G and J also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MHN and attention formulations, dynamical-system equations, and metric definitions in Equations 1–27 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and Section 6 retain the same claims about residual-based calibration without uncertainty propagation and benchmarking existing propagation methods for multi-step calibration.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the trajectory-length limitation and discussion of sequence-length tuning and alternative training objectives. Appendix J retains the same interpretation linking calibration to capturing non-Gaussian predictive distributions.

D1.justification: The architecture and memory details, context features, PyTorch pseudocode, data-generation parameters, and tuned hyperparameters are unchanged. No code or data access information is added, removed, or revised.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 7, and positioning relative to Auer et al. (2023) and ensemble methods are unchanged. The Kingma et al. (2015) citation merely moves from page 2 to page 1.

P1.justification: V2 removes the first-page notice stating that the work is preliminary, under ICML review, and not to be distributed, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing the first-page notice causes limited text reflow on pages 1–2, including moving a citation across the page break. Tables 1–4, Figures 1–6, and all rendered pages 3–22 are identical.

improvement.justification: V2 changes publication-status text and slightly reflows the opening pages. The scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, including all appendices. These cosmetic edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
